title: Gradient Descent on a 1D Quadratic

paper.title: An overview of gradient descent optimization algorithms

hook: Watch a ball roll down a parabola. If the step size is too big, it flies away!

explorations.title: Convergence vs divergence
explorations.observe: With \eta=0.1, \theta shrinks to 0. With \eta=1.2, \theta grows without bound.
explorations.why: The update multiplies \theta by (1-2\eta). If |1-2\eta|<1, it shrinks; if >1, it grows.

explorations.title: One-step convergence at \eta=0.5
explorations.predict: Can we reach the minimum in one step?
explorations.why: When \eta=0.5, the factor (1-2\eta) is zero, so \theta_1 = 0.

limitation: This demo uses a simple 1D quadratic where the gradient is exactly 2\theta. Real loss surfaces are high-dimensional and non-convex, so convergence depends on more than just the learning rate.
misconception: A larger learning rate always speeds up convergence. In reality, if \eta > 1, the iterates diverge.

claims.text: Gradient descent updates parameters by subtracting the learning rate times the gradient.

outcomes.outcome: Explain the gradient descent update rule.
Predict convergence or divergence based on the learning rate.
Verify that \eta=0.5 reaches the minimum in one step.
